title: How LinkedIn Built a View-Agnostic Analytics System for Modern iOS UI Architectures
gist: LinkedIn built a view-agnostic iOS analytics system around a shared MeasurableNode contract (identity, geometry, hierarchy, lifecycle) so that virtual UI nodes that never become UIViews can still be measured alongside UIKit views. The design allows gradual adoption, and the approach is presented as applicable to apps mixing UIKit, SwiftUI and cross-platform layout engines.

insights.claim: Modern iOS UI architectures increasingly use flattened layouts and custom rendering where cards, sections and containers are virtual nodes that never materialize as UIViews, so UIKit-only analytics can miss impressions, lose hierarchy, miscalculate visibility and misattribute user actions.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Mobile analytics/telemetry vendors built on view hierarchies face accuracy gaps as UI frameworks evolve.
insights.locator: As LinkedIn senior software engineer Keerthana

insights.claim: LinkedIn found the assumption that everything is a UIView deeply embedded in its codebase, including helper code walking superviews, visibility checks reading view frames, and cleanup tied to view removal, all of which had to be found and updated.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Shows the hidden migration cost of UI framework modernization in large apps.
insights.quote: helper code that walked superviews, visibility checks that read frames directly from views, cleanup logic tied to view removal
insights.locator: LinkedIn engineers encountered three main challenges

insights.claim: LinkedIn's MeasurableNode contract relaxes the requirement that every measurable element be a UIView by exposing four properties, identity, geometry, hierarchy and lifecycle, so UIViews and virtual nodes share one analytics system.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Contract-based telemetry decouples analytics from rendering technology.
insights.locator: LinkedIn's solution introduces a shared MeasurableNode

insights.claim: In LinkedIn's design, attach and detach methods let the rendering system notify analytics when a node attaches, its frame changes, or it detaches, since UIKit sends lifecycle notifications only to UIViews; the framework must also traverse the hybrid hierarchy to attribute gestures to virtual nodes.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Lifecycle discipline must be enforced at the framework level for analytics correctness.
insights.quote: when a node attaches, when its frame changes, and when it detaches
insights.locator: The attach and detach methods are central

insights.claim: LinkedIn's view-agnostic analytics design enables gradual adoption, letting teams modernize one part of the UI while existing view-based analytics keep working.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Incremental migration lowers the risk and cost of UI modernization in large consumer apps.
insights.quote: Teams can modernize one part of the UI without rewriting everything around it.

insights.claim: LinkedIn's engineers had to balance short-term compatibility against long-term correctness and enforce attach/detach discipline at the framework level when building view-agnostic analytics.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Highlights governance requirements for cross-cutting telemetry changes.

insights.claim: A view-agnostic analytics model based on a shared contract has broader applicability beyond UIKit because many apps now mix UIKit with SwiftUI, cross-platform layout engines or hybrid solutions.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Fragmented UI stacks create demand for rendering-agnostic product analytics.
